description: `dependencyDashboardApproval`: nothing opens until its dashboard box is checked; `automerge` then finishes it once required checks pass on `main`'s ruleset.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: `chore` is hidden in Release Please's changelog sections and cuts no release; `fix` makes a security update a patch release on its own. These skip dashboard approval, so a person merges them.

customManagers.description: Bare versions annotated with a renovate comment (GitHub Actions inputs)

packageRules.description: Renovate reports no release timestamp for a digest, so the soak would stay pending forever. The SHA pin plus reading the diff guards these.
Fallback for mise tools without a rule of their own (python and uv are regrouped below). No mise.lock, so lock file maintenance has nothing to refresh.
Most constraints are open `>=`, so the default strategy proposes nothing; `update-lockfile` makes in-range upgrades arrive as named PRs touching `uv.lock`.
`uv lock --upgrade-package` takes no version and resolves the newest release regardless of the soak, so the soak would only fail the artifact update (renovatebot/renovate#41624).
Bounded to one minor in pyproject.toml; kept apart so new diagnostics are attributable to the PR that introduced them.

mise.toml and setup-uv's `python-version`/`version` in CI. One group, because CI's uv must know the Python it is asked to download. Matching is on packageName (`python/cpython`, `astral-sh/uv` for mise). No soak: it would apply to only some datasources and split the group.
